summary.text: 15-year-old male with a history of regular sea swimming for the past 8 months and no other acute or chronic disease, presenting to an otorhinolaryngology outpatient clinic with persistent left-sided otorrhea and hearing impairment despite multiple courses of topical empirical ciprofloxacin; CSOM.

Otoscopy showed tympanic membrane perforation with purulent discharge. Ear discharge was collected with three swabs; aerobic culture grew a mixed culture of Achromobacter spp. and V. parahaemolyticus identified by MALDI-TOF MS. On VITEK 2 testing the Achromobacter spp. isolate was multidrug resistant and susceptible only to carbapenems, and V. parahaemolyticus was susceptible to fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines. Table 1 lists no results for the anaerobic and fungal swabs.
Topical ciprofloxacin was changed; the patient received a systemic carbapenem and an oral fluoroquinolone for three weeks, during which clinical improvement was observed.

ambiguities.issue: The authors speculate that V. parahaemolyticus is plausibly linked to seawater exposure and that Achromobacter spp. may be an opportunistic colonizer favored by prior antibiotic courses; the case report does not establish the source or the pathogenic role of either organism.

evidence.quote: The isolation of V. parahaemolyticus in this case is plausibly linked to the patient’s repeated exposure to seawater
Achromobacter spp. may represent an opportunistic colonizer favored by prior broad-spectrum antibiotic courses

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a confirmed environmental source, colonization, or causal role of either organism, nor broad-spectrum antibiotic courses (the case text names topical ciprofloxacin only).

ambiguities.issue: MALDI-TOF MS identified the Achromobacter isolate as A. xylosoxidans, but the authors report it as Achromobacter spp. because the method cannot reliably discriminate closely related species.
